value: I understand this identity will be removed from this device.

value: Could not forget the identity. Try again.

reason: One step-counter sentence for every multi-step flow, so "Step 2 of 3" reads the same wherever it appears (myne-md/myne#871). The keys stay separate because the vocabularies are: vault creation's steps are enumerated in stepOrder.ts, these are the invite wizards', and the value is the sentence only rather than a shared component.

value: Save your identity phrase
reason: The phrase step of the identity ceremony is one screen on both clients (myne-md/myne#869 split it off the type-back step), so its title is the same title; two wordings would name the same step differently on the phone and on the desktop.

value: Enter these four words from the identity phrase you just saved.
reason: The desktop identity-setup dialog and the mobile identity flow run the SAME phrase-typeback step, so the question a user must answer is one sentence. Rewording per client would let the two clients ask a different question about the same phrase.

value: That does not match word #{{pos}}.
reason: The mismatch line for that same typeback step, on the desktop identity-setup dialog and the mobile identity flow; one step, two clients, and the position placeholder interpolates identically on both.

value: Your identity is not signed in on this device. Unlock your identity and try again.
reason: Same state and the same remedy on the accept and the join: the person identity is not signed in on this device, so neither command can proceed and both tell the user to unlock it. The two KEYS stay separate on purpose (the mappings are two modules, decisions/protocol/0672), so a copy edit on one cannot silently move the other; the sentence is shared because the fact is one fact, not because the errors are the same error.
